page.layout: One printed page, one text block in two parallel columns under a full-width title; the stanzas run left column first, then right column. Notes in the margin: one short note at lower right ("Nolo") beside the last line of the right column.

main_text.head: PARAPHRASIS PSALMI LI. MISERERE mei Deus.
main_text.p: QVO mereatu sordido Contaminatus perdite Vertâmeæ quæ nescia Labis latebra me tegeti

p.i: Tellus, mare, æther, conscij Redarguunt me criminis, In me, miser, nescrie & Deum quod admisi meum.
Eheu, meis erroribus Quis tristibus medebitur? Nu terra, potus aut polus? Res nulla certè condita.
Virtute diffisus mea, Virtute confisus tua: Ad te unicum fidelium Sotera nunc me confero.
Miserere fracti, mi Deus, Miserere, crimen expia, Tuam secundum gratiam Nullo reuinctam termino.
Purga usque & usque noxio Mesospicator crimine: Fœdasq; peccati eluè Labes beato nectare.
Heu, perpetratum d me scelus Agnosco, fateor, & gemo; Et usque tetra mentibus Imago culpæ se ingeris.
Tibi tibi soli, miser, Peccaui, ut æquus omnibus Probère iudex, funditus Si me reum exstirpaueris
Corrupit heu medullitus Me criminis contagio: Mecumq; prauitas sata, Parentis aruo prodiit.
At nuda semper veritas Tibi placet iubar tuæ Multos latens sapientiæ Mentis mihi umbram discutit.
Lustralis hyssopi meum Fronde expia piaculum, Niue hoc pudendum dedecus Vt purius respl ēdeat.
Cœlestis aura gaudij Irroret aruum pectoris Mei, uigorem pristinum Contrita membra ut sentiant.
Eia, à meis erroribus Auerte uultum: me in reos Merito relatum de tuis Tabulis benignus exime.
Ah mi Deus cor squalidùm Intaminatum sordibus In me crea: sanctos mihi Mentis recessius integra.Nolo

page.notes: Right column line 15 ends "integra." with the note "Nolo" set in the right margin at the foot; read as printed. Several letters are worn and uncertain (for example "nescrie", "Nu terra", "Mesospicator", "respl ēdeat"); these are left as I read them without [?] marks because the scan is faint at those points and the readings are provisional. The printed title "rere mei Deus" is the second line of the title, read as part of the head.
